description: The galaxy's foremost peacekeepers, devoted to the light side and the will of the Force.
Ancient Force order on Tython that sought balance between the light (Ashla) and the dark (Bogan), before the Jedi and the Sith existed.
Force-sensitives who channel prophetic visions and healing without Jedi or Sith alignment.
Isolationist survivors who developed fierce independence and telekinetic mastery.
Scholarly diplomats blending Force philosophy with negotiation and intellectual pursuit.
Pacifist users of the White Current, specialising in illusion and concealment.
Reclusive aliens who see the Force as a flowing river; practice spatial teleportation.
Unaffiliated Force-users who channel the Force through rigorous physical discipline.

A reclusive, patriotic sect of the Jedi Order based on Corellia that prized loyalty to their homeworld over the Republic, permitted marriage and hereditary bloodlines, stayed largely independent from the main Jedi Order and viewed with suspicion by the Jedi High Council.
Embodiment of the Force's central path, dwelling in tension between light and dark. Canon-only name, kept as SL100 homebrew.
Independents who walk between light and dark, rejecting dogmatic Jedi or Sith extremes.
Heretical philosophy holding the Force is inherently good; the dark side is mere misuse.
Ancient Force-sensitive warriors who rejected the emerging Jedi Order to stay independent.
Honour-bound warriors connected to the Ashla, a Force tradition outside Jedi/Sith lineage. Canon-only name, kept as SL100 homebrew. See Lasan.
The ancient enemy of the Jedi, driven by passion, power, and the Rule of Two.
Pre-Rule of Two Sith factions commanding armies through raw dark side dominance.
Matriarchal witches wielding dark-side magick drawn from Dathomir's Force nexus.
Dark side agents of the Empire, trained by Vader to hunt post-Order 66 Jedi survivors.
Fanatical dark side seers serving Palpatine as interpreters of Sith prophecy.
Fallen Jedi who embraced the dark side independently, outside formal Sith lineage.
A cult dedicated to resurrecting Sith Lord Marka Ragnos by siphoning Force nexus energy.
Dark side assassins embedded within Tapani nobility, blending poison craft with Force.
The democratic union of member worlds ruled from Coruscant by the Senate and the Supreme Chancellor, and defended for most of its history by the Jedi.
The Separatists: systems and corporations that seceded from the Republic under Count Dooku and fought the Clone Wars.
Palpatine's New Order, which replaced the Republic and ruled through fear, the Imperial military and the Emperor's agents.
The Rebel Alliance, joined by the Corellian Treaty, which fought the Galactic Civil War against the Empire.
The successor to the Rebel Alliance, governing from Coruscant after its liberation.
The Imperial state left in the Deep Core and the Outer Rim after Endor, later reunified under Pellaeon.
The Galactic Alliance, reorganised from the New Republic during the Yuuzhan Vong War.
The Imperial Remnant reborn under Emperor Roan Fel.
Matriarchal cluster of 63 worlds behind the Transitory Mists, closed to outsiders for millennia.
era: c. 4000 BBY onward (opened to the galaxy 8 ABY)

description: The disciplined, defensive state of the Chiss in the Unknown Regions.
Corporate-run sector of hundreds of systems on the galactic rim, where profit is law.
The trade cartel whose blockade of Naboo began the fall of the Republic; later a pillar of the Separatists.

faction: Techno Union, InterGalactic Banking Clan and Commerce Guild
description: Separatist industrial guilds and financiers that built and paid for the droid armies.
The Republic's standing army and fleet before the Ruusan Reformation; revived as the Grand Army.
The Republic's intelligence service in the Great Galactic War and the Cold War that followed.
Non-Force-sensitive auxiliaries who supported the Jedi in the field.
The guardians of the Senate and the Chancellor.
The clone army of the Republic, commanded by Jedi generals in the Clone Wars.
Corellia's planetary police (CorSec), famous for its stubborn independence.
era: Before 3660 BBY onward (dissolved 7 ABY, refounded by 26 ABY)

description: The Empire's fleet of Star Destroyers, TIE wings and line officers.
The Empire's ground forces: walkers, artillery and garrison troops.
The Emperor's elite troops, loyal beyond question.
The ISB, the Empire's secret police, watching for sedition in the military and the population.
The Empire's foreign intelligence service of spies, analysts and assassins.
The Rebel Alliance's intelligence network of spies, slicers and safe houses.
The Rebel Alliance's commandos and Special Operations teams.
The Rebellion's elite starfighter squadron, led by Luke Skywalker and later Wedge Antilles.
The New Republic's intelligence service, successor to Alliance Intelligence.
The Bothan information-brokering network that sells to anyone who can pay.
Jacen Solo's secret police within the Galactic Alliance.
The clan-based warrior culture, open to any species that adopts the Mandalorian way of life.
Religious warrior clans who crusaded across the galaxy and allied with the Sith in the Great Sith War.
The Crusaders reborn under Mandalore the Ultimate, who fought the Mandalorian Wars against the Republic.
Jaster Mereel's mercenaries, who held to his Supercommando Codex until Galidraan.
Tor Vizsla's splinter faction that sought a return to the old crusading ways.
Mandalorian supercommandos who fought for the Republic and later defended Mandalore against the Empire.
era: Clone Wars to Galactic Civil War (c. 22 BBY–4 ABY)

description: Vast criminal empire controlled by the Hutt species, dominating smuggling, slavery, and gambling across the Outer Rim.
One of the most powerful criminal syndicates in the galaxy, with cells on nearly every inhabited world and deep political corruption.
Aggressive underworld faction led by Tyber Zann, built on blackmail, corruption, and theft of Imperial superweapons.
Influential criminal organisation with ties to the Republic and early Empire, involved in spice and contraband trafficking.
Sprawling crime network rivalling the Hutts, dealing in slavery, bounty hunting, and illegal trade across the Mid and Outer Rim.
Secretive assassins' guild operating behind a legitimate bounty hunter front, answering to shadowy hidden masters.
Pirate gang operating in the Outer Rim, preying on freighters and merchant convoys.
Loose confederation of pirate captains and mercenaries operating near the Maw cluster.
Organised slaving guild with licensed hunters and established trade routes, primarily active in the Outer Rim.
Black-market trading ring dealing in Force artefacts, forbidden technology, and stolen Imperial data.
Loose coalition of independent smugglers formed to resist both Imperial crackdowns and Hutt dominance.
Spice-trafficking cartel controlling the kessel spice trade, willing to use political murder to protect market share.
Smuggling gang based on Kijimi, dealing in spice and stolen goods throughout the Outer Rim. Canon-only name, kept as SL100 homebrew.
Ancient slaving empire of the Zygerrian species, revived under Separatist patronage during the Clone Wars.
Fraudulent religious organisation secretly enslaving pilgrims to work Ylesian spice mines for the Hutts.
Forced-labour operation producing glitterstim spice, controlled variously by Hutts, the Empire, and criminal brokers.
The galaxy-spanning professional body regulating bounty hunting contracts, licensing, and disputes between hunters.
Elite bounty hunters drawing on Mandalorian warrior culture, feared for their skill and beskar armour.
A prestigious bounty hunter house known for selective clientele and high-value political targets.
Mid-tier bounty hunter house specialising in skip tracing and debt collection for corporate clients.
Criminal organisation doubling as a bounty broker, connecting clients with hunters throughout the Mid Rim.
Professional body for hired killers, operating under a loose code that nominally prohibited targeting innocents.
The galaxy's premier capital ship builder; produced Star Destroyers, Victory-class, and Imperial-class vessels for the Republic and Empire.
Produced the distinctive organic-hulled Mon Cal cruisers that became the backbone of the Rebel and New Republic fleets.
Ancient shipbuilder responsible for the Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser and numerous Republic warships.
Early Republic-era megacorporation producing heavy warships during the Alsakan Conflicts. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article. See Alsakan.
Produced Strike-class cruisers and remotely piloted warship systems for the Empire and successor states.
Built the Carrack-class light cruiser and various Imperial patrol vessels favoured for anti-smuggling operations.
Designed and built the TIE fighter series and numerous Imperial starfighters and shuttles.
Produced the legendary X-wing T-65 and T-47 airspeeder; key supplier to the Rebel Alliance.
Co-designed the Z-95 Headhunter with Incom; produced various starfighters for Republic and civilian markets. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article.
New Republic-aligned starfighter manufacturer producing the E-wing escort fighter.
Produced the GR-75 medium transport widely used by the Rebel Alliance; went bankrupt under Imperial pressure.
Prolific shipbuilder producing the Millennium Falcon's YT series, CR90 corvettes, and countless civilian freighters.
Mandalorian shipbuilder producing the Pursuer-class enforcement ship and various combat-capable vessels.
Produced repulsorlift craft, luxury yachts, and combat skiffs widely used across the galaxy.
Dominant blaster manufacturer supplying both the Empire and Rebel Alliance; produced the DL-44 and E-11 among hundreds of models.
Major weapons conglomerate producing blasters, grenades, missile systems, and the PLX rocket launcher.
Ancient megacorporation dealing in weapons, slave labour, and colonisation; deeply corrupt and influential across many eras.
Imperial-aligned industrial giant producing mining equipment repurposed as weapons platforms and military hardware.
Produced Imperial probe droids, Viper probe droids, and various autonomous weapons platforms.
Separatist-aligned manufacturer of battle droids, AATs, and droid starfighters for the Confederacy of Independent Systems.
Built the Separatist Vulture droid starfighter and various droid-crewed combat craft.
Kuat Drive Yards subsidiary that designed the AT-TE walker, LAAT gunship, and other Republic ground and air assets.
Produced heavy turbolaser batteries and weapons systems integrated into Corellian-built capital ships.
Sienar subsidiary producing electronic warfare suites, sensor arrays, and classified weapons for the Empire.
Sole producers of the Republic Grand Army clone troopers; engineered, grew, and trained millions of soldiers from Jango Fett's template.
Manufactured Spaarti cloning cylinders capable of rapid clone production; used by Grand Admiral Thrawn to quickly rebuild Imperial forces.
Pioneered controversial genetic engineering of sentient species; produced Arkanian hybrids as a slave labour and combat workforce.
Colicoid-run manufacturer producing the Droideka destroyer droid and other lethal autonomous weapons for the Separatists.
Biotech and droid megacorp involved in experimental lifeform modification and illegal cloning operations. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article.
Geonosian-operated foundries that mass-produced Separatist battle droids and super battle droids at industrial scale. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article. See Geonosis.
The Empire's primary R&D body overseeing the Death Star project, superlaser technology, and classified superweapon programmes.
Top-secret Imperial research base inside the Maw cluster; birthplace of the Death Star prototype and the Sun Crusher.
Parent conglomerate of Sienar Fleet Systems; involved in classified weapons research under Imperial contract.
New Republic-era defence contractor involved in hyperdrive research and experimental long-range weapons systems.
Pre-Imperial predecessor to Sienar Fleet Systems; designed early starfighter prototypes that evolved into the TIE line.

The Empire's central naval construction authority overseeing all Star Destroyer and capital ship production across Kuat, Fondor, and other yards. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article. See Imperial Navy.
Major Imperial fleet construction facility producing Star Destroyers and Super Star Destroyers alongside Kuat Drive Yards.
Secret Imperial Deep Core shipyards producing Eclipse-class Super Star Destroyers and World Devastators for Palpatine's reborn forces.
Key Imperial repair and construction facility; site of the climactic battle of the Thrawn campaign and New Republic operations.
Imperial orbital construction facility producing mid-tier capital ships and replenishment vessels for the Core Worlds fleet. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article. See Corulag.
Imperial-controlled yards at Sullust producing landing craft, assault ships, and support vessels for invasion operations.
Remote Imperial facility producing Victory-class Star Destroyers and escort vessels away from Rebel interdiction. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article. See Scarl.
Major Imperial Remnant fleet yard; one of the last functioning heavy construction facilities after Endor.
Administrative body coordinating TIE fighter procurement, variant development, and fleet-wide starfighter logistics. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article.
Primary TIE series manufacturer under exclusive Imperial contract; produced TIE/ln, TIE Interceptor, TIE Bomber, and Defender variants.
Produced the Lambda-class shuttle, Sentinel-class landing craft, and various Imperial transport and command vessels.
Manufactured Imperial dropships, assault shuttles, and the gamma-class assault shuttle for ground assault operations.
Parent conglomerate controlling Sienar Fleet Systems; held classified development contracts for next-generation Imperial starfighters.
The Empire's apex weapons R&D authority, overseeing the Death Star superlaser, turbolaser development, and all classified ordnance programmes.
Top-secret research base hidden inside the Maw black hole cluster; produced the Death Star prototype, the Sun Crusher, and the World Devastator.
Coordinated field testing, procurement, and standardisation of Imperial small arms, heavy weapons, and vehicle-mounted ordnance. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article.
Classified Imperial bioweapons research station that developed an experimental virus causing the dead to reanimate. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article. See Blackwing virus outbreak on Dathomir.
Broad research arm overseeing non-military science alongside classified weapons physics and superweapon feasibility studies.
Elite Imperial think-tank driving the Death Star project and advanced weapons concepts under Grand Moff Tarkin's direct patronage. Canon-only name, kept as SL100 homebrew.
Engineering programme producing Torpedo Sphere platforms designed to overwhelm planetary shields for orbital bombardment. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article. See Torpedo Sphere.
Managed procurement and production of all Imperial ground vehicles including AT-ATs, AT-STs, and repulsorlift platforms. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article. See Imperial Army.
KDY subsidiary retained by the Empire to continue AT-TE derivatives and develop new walker platforms post-Clone Wars.
KDY's ground-vehicle arm producing the AT-AT and associated heavy walker platforms for Imperial planetary assault.
Oversaw production and standardisation of stormtrooper armour, weapons loadouts, and specialised trooper variant equipment. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article.
Produced 74-Z speeder bikes and Imperial repulsorlift scout vehicles under exclusive military contracts.
Post-Clone Wars Imperial operation retaining Kaminoan facilities to produce stormtrooper clones and experimental elite soldiers. SL100 homebrew: no Legends article. See Kamino.
Palpatine's secret Wayland storehouse operation using Spaarti cylinders to rapidly produce a new clone army for the Empire's resurgence.
Palpatine's hidden citadel on Wayland housing cloning equipment, Force-adept clone experiments, and the Emperor's most secret projects.
Classified branch conducting research into biological and chemical weapons, including Project Blackwing and other containment-failure incidents.
Grand Admiral Thrawn's reactivation of Spaarti cylinders on Wayland to produce an accelerated clone army for his campaign against the New Republic.
